title: Fifth Plenum + Electronics testing ban + Falling share prices
gist: MERICS China Essentials covering the CCP fifth plenum (only 279 Central Committee members attended vs 376 selected in 2022, a new resolution tightening loyalty/performance discipline, unusual promotions and PLA passes-over), the FCC's expansion of 'Bad Labs' rules to ban all China-based electronics testing for US-bound devices, and the PBOC's intervention after the CSI300's steepest monthly drop in a decade (-8.5% in October). A digest adds weak PMI (48.7), record population decline, and the first drop in fiscal revenue.

themes.theme: Fifth plenum: purges and loyalty drive

insights.claim: Only 279 members of the CCP Central Committee attended the October 26-29, 2026 fifth plenum, down from the 376 officials selected in 2022, reflecting personnel gaps left by anti-corruption campaigns.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Scale of elite attrition signals ongoing political instability and governance-capacity risk heading into the 2027 Congress.
insights.quote: The CCP gathered 279 members of the Central Committee for its fifth plenary session on October 26-29, down from the 376 officials selected in 2022

insights.claim: According to MERICS's Daria Impiombato, the fifth plenum saw the lowest turnout of the post-Mao era, with around a quarter of Central Committee members absent, indicating the scale of recent CCP purges.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Purge intensity is historically extreme; expect continued policy-implementation caution among officials.
insights.quote: around a quarter of all Central Committee members did not attend

insights.claim: The plenum's resolution on 'full and rigorous party self-governance' signals the discipline campaign is far from complete, focusing on cadres unwilling or unable to deliver on policy, checks on powerful central officials, and a perceived lack of 'party spirit' among younger officials.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Further purges are likely; policy execution risk from risk-averse cadres persists.
insights.quote: makes clear that the campaign to strengthen discipline is far from complete

insights.claim: The resolution formally elevates Xi Jinping's 'thought on party building' and portrays him as having rescued the party from internal corrosion and a fading grasp on power.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Further ideological consolidation around Xi reduces odds of policy pivots driven by factional balance.

insights.claim: Xi's governance model contains built-in contradictions: efforts to reduce formalism add more oversight and bureaucracy, cadres must innovate only within approved boundaries after authorization, and may voice concerns but not challenge the center.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: These tensions suggest bureaucratic paralysis and slower local policy responsiveness, including on stimulus delivery.
insights.quote: Efforts to reduce formalism rely on additional layers of oversight and bureaucracy.
insights.locator: At the same time, the document

insights.claim: MERICS's Katja Drinhausen argues Xi's purges are a matter of ideological conviction, not just power maintenance, and that Europe should not expect Beijing to compromise more while it focuses on internal party issues; instead cadres will rush to demonstrate dedication to national interests.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Expect assertive Chinese external posture in 2027 trade and geopolitical negotiations with the EU.
insights.quote: it should expect China to continue to assert itself resolutely as cadres rush to demonstrate their dedication to national interests

insights.claim: The plenum formally ratified expulsions of former Xinjiang Party Secretary Ma Xingrui, top PLA generals Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli, and former International Department head Liu Jianchao, showing purges are reaching China's foreign relations apparatus.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Purges of military and foreign-affairs elites raise questions about PLA readiness and China's diplomatic capacity.
insights.quote: confirms the growing impact of the purges on China’s foreign relations apparatus

insights.claim: MERICS warns that while purges may reinforce Xi's control, they risk creating a climate of fear and uncertainty and raise questions about the institutional capacity of the Chinese state.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Institutional capacity erosion is a tail risk for policy execution and crisis management in China.
insights.quote: they also risk creating a climate of fear and uncertainty inside and raise questions about the institutional capacity of the state

themes.theme: Personnel signals: PLA passed over, younger civilians promoted

insights.claim: Ten alternate members were promoted to full CCP Central Committee membership at the fifth plenum, but some contenders by vote ranking, including PLA and People's Armed Police officials, were passed over, signaling unusual maneuvering or possible further purges in the security apparatus.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Watch for further security-apparatus purges; PLA leadership instability is a geopolitical risk variable (e.g., Taiwan timelines).
insights.quote: signaling either unusual political maneuvering or possible further purges in China’s security apparatus

insights.claim: All ten promoted alternate members were civilians, including provincial deputy party secretaries in their early 50s, signaling Beijing is cultivating a younger cohort for senior posts; one is Zhejiang governor Liu Jie, from Xi Jinping's former power base.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Early identification of rising officials helps anticipate the post-2027 leadership line-up.
insights.locator: But as officials were pushed out

insights.claim: General Zhang Shengmin was promoted to the Politburo outside a Party Congress at age 68, above the customary 67 age limit; MERICS suggests this may relate to a potential restructuring or restocking of the Central Military Commission, with possible retirement at next year's Congress.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: CMC restructuring could reshape PLA command; relevant to cross-strait risk assessment.
insights.locator: The Plenum promoted General Zhang Shengmin

insights.claim: The fact that no PLA officer was promoted to full Central Committee membership suggests Xi Jinping is in no rush to fill vacant positions and the post-purge generational transition in the military may take time.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Prolonged PLA leadership vacuums imply lower near-term readiness for major military operations.
insights.quote: Xi Jinping is in no rush to fill vacant positions
insights.locator: The Plenum promoted General Zhang Shengmin

insights.claim: The resolution reflects leadership anxieties about the beliefs of younger cadres born after 1978, with intensified ideological education aimed at forging loyalty to Xi so his legacy outlasts him; MERICS questions whether this will work once that generation rises.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Long-term ideological drift among future leaders is a generational political-risk wildcard.
insights.locator: But as officials were pushed out

themes.theme: US FCC ban on China-based electronics testing

insights.claim: 82% of electronic devices entering the US market pass through testing labs in China, which the expanded US FCC 'Bad Labs' ban will now exclude.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Massive compliance shift: testing capacity outside China becomes a bottleneck and pricing-power opportunity.
insights.quote: which 82% of devices entering the US market pass through
insights.locator: Wider US ban on Chinese electronics testing

insights.claim: The FCC expanded its 2025 'Bad Labs' rules from government-controlled labs to all testing facilities in countries lacking a Mutual Recognition Agreement with the US, meaning US-bound devices must be tested outside China, with a two-year transition period.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Two-year clock for electronics OEMs to re-route certification; watch MRA-country labs.
insights.locator: Wider US ban on Chinese electronics testing

insights.claim: Manufacturers are expected to face supply chain delays and higher compliance costs from the FCC testing ban, as alternatives to Chinese testing providers are likely more expensive.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Margin headwind for consumer electronics makers exporting to the US.

insights.claim: The FCC ban hits Chinese subsidiaries of European testing firms like TÜV Rheinland and Eurofins, but could create opportunities for European labs as testing and certification demand shifts to other markets.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Testing, inspection and certification players with non-China capacity (e.g., Eurofins) could gain share; China-heavy operations at risk.
insights.quote: it may also create opportunities for European laboratories as demand for testing and certification services shifts to other markets

insights.claim: China's Ministry of Commerce criticized the expanded FCC testing ban and warned Beijing could take countermeasures.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Retaliation risk for US firms in China; another front in US-China tech escalation.
insights.locator: Wider US ban on Chinese electronics testing

themes.theme: China equity slump and PBOC intervention

insights.claim: China's benchmark CSI300 fell 8.5% in October 2026, its steepest decline in a decade, driven by AI-bubble jitters and a sluggish economy.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Signals fragility of the AI-led China equity rally; policy put now in play.
insights.quote: China’s benchmark CSI300 saw its steepest decline in a decade, falling 8.5 percent in October.

insights.claim: The PBOC deployed over CNY 100 billion (EUR 13.5 billion) in swaps with financial institutions and made permanent a relending scheme for share buybacks and purchases, cutting its rate to 1% from 1.25%.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: A permanent, cheaper equity-support facility is a structural 'state put' under Chinese stocks.
insights.quote: made permanent a relending scheme for share buybacks and purchases, cutting the interest rate to 1 percent from 1.25 percent

insights.claim: Beijing depends on capital markets to finance innovative and high-tech sectors, particularly the AI innovation chain under 'new quality productive forces,' so market stability is a strategic priority rather than just a financial one.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Expect continued state intervention to support tech/AI equities; policy backstops shape positioning.

insights.claim: With China's real estate collapse and capital outflow limits leaving few options, households have turned to stocks, making the market significantly household-driven and steep losses likely to further weigh on consumer confidence and demand regardless of PBOC stabilization.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Equity wealth effect now matters for Chinese consumption; bearish read for consumer demand.
insights.quote: The steep losses will likely further weigh on overall consumer confidence and demand, regardless of whether the PBOC’s intervention can stabilize the market

insights.claim: MERICS's Sophia Pradels argues the market correction reflects the eroding avenues for China's middle-class households to maintain and build wealth amid persistent stagnation, widening imbalances and low consumer confidence.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Structural headwind to China consumption rebalancing thesis.
insights.quote: the avenues left to maintain and build wealth are eroding

themes.theme: Macro digest: exports, demographics, fiscal stress

insights.claim: China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 48.7 in October 2026 from 50.0 in September, driven by weaker new export orders as trading partners raised concerns over widening trade deficits with China.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Export-led growth meeting partner pushback; downside risk to Q4 growth.
insights.quote: fell to 48.7 in October from 50.0 in September

insights.claim: China's prolonged property downturn is dragging on domestic consumption and pushing firms to rely more heavily on exports, which in turn fuels trade-partner backlash.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Feedback loop raises protectionism risk in EU and elsewhere.

insights.claim: China's population fell for a fourth consecutive year in 2025, by a record 3.39 million.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Demographic decline underpins long-term growth and consumption headwinds.

insights.claim: China's general public budget revenue dropped for the first time in September 2026, intensifying financial pressure on local governments amid the property slump.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Local-government fiscal stress constrains stimulus capacity; watch LGFV risk.

insights.claim: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said at Peking University that Germany does not want to decouple from China but wants fairer economic relations and reduced trade imbalances, while Xi Jinping urged Germany toward a 'rational, pragmatic and friendly' stance.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Germany-China relations remain engage-but-hedge; trade-imbalance friction persists.
insights.locator: Germany does not want China decoupling
